# using-git-worktrees: PR-head base-merge outcomes for acme/widget#82 I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace. The caller passed resolved PR values, so I follow `reference/pr-head.md` instead of Steps 0 and 1. ## Aliases | Alias | Value | |---|---| | ROOT | /work/widget | | W | /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry (`` = fix-retry) | | A | aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa (headRefOid, PRE_REWORK_HEAD) | | B | bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb (BASE_SHA) | | E | eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee | The session cwd never changes, including in done-green, where it stays at /work/widget/.worktrees/other. Every command uses `git -C` on ROOT or W. ## Shared setup (identical in every row) 1. `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir`. Both return /work/widget/.git, so ROOT = ROOT. 2. `git -C ROOT rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` returns empty, so this is not a submodule. 3. `git -C ROOT fetch origin`. 4. `git -C ROOT rev-parse --verify -q A^{commit}` succeeds, and origin/fix/retry = A. 5. `git -C ROOT rev-parse origin/main` returns B. 6. All stops pass: - isCrossRepository is false. - `git -C ROOT worktree list --porcelain` shows fix/retry only at W. - The head is reachable. 7. Provisioning row "home already on headRefName": - `git -C W status --porcelain` is clean. - `git -C W merge --ff-only origin/fix/retry`. - `git -C W rev-parse HEAD` returns A. ## Merge legend | Code | Command / rule | |---|---| | M | `git -C W merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main` | | P | `git -C W merge-base --is-ancestor A HEAD` must exit 0 after every outcome | | T | Threads query from the reference, run once for #82 with o=acme r=widget n=82. It succeeds empty, giving `Threads: none`. | | R | Step 4 report, below | **R (Step 4 report):** ``` Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry Branch: fix/retry Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa PR: acme/widget#82 Pre-rework head: A Base SHA: bbbbbbb ``` ## Helper legend (conflict rows) | Step | Action | |---|---| | H1 | Read the overrides from B, not the conflicted tree: `git -C ROOT show B:.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md`. Then derive SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS. | | H2 | Snapshot status: `git -C W status --porcelain` returns `UU src/retry.ts`. | | H3 | `git -C W diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` returns `src/retry.ts`. | | H4 | Dispatch one fresh foreground `implementer` (`cwd: W`, `async: false`) with the tuple (conflict-list=[src/retry.ts], fetched-base=origin/main@B, SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS=['node --test test/retry.test.mjs']). The helper must resolve preserving both sides, run exactly those commands, and `git -C W add src/retry.ts`. It must not commit, abort, or edit outside the list. | | H5 | Completion checks, all required:
• `git -C W diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` is empty.
• `git -C W diff --cached --name-only` includes src/retry.ts.
• `git -C W status --porcelain` delta is contained in [src/retry.ts]. | | H6 | The orchestrator, never the helper, runs `git -C W commit --no-edit`. HEAD becomes E. | | HX | On any failure: `git -C W merge --abort`. Record `merge: unresolved - src/retry.ts` and continue on A. The spec Design opens with `merge origin/main and resolve src/retry.ts` as eventual Task 1. | Constraints are read at B in every row and are authoritative over the worktree copies. No other pre-approval tests, reviewers, or push. ## Outcome rows (each independent) | Row | Delta | Merge record | |---|---|---| | noop | M reports base already an ancestor. No commit. HEAD = A. Then P, T, R. | `merge: no-op - head contains origin/main` | | clean | M succeeds and creates E as the first rework commit. Then P (A is an ancestor of E), T, R. | `merge: eeeeeee` | | done-green | M conflicts. H1 finds `node --test ` under PR gate with requires credentials: false, so the scoped command is the tuple's. H2–H4 run; the helper returns `done`. The scoped test passes. H5 passes, H6 commits E. Then P, T, R. | `merge: eeeeeee, 1 file(s) resolved, scoped tests green` | | exception-red | Same as done-green, but the helper returns `done - contract exception: retry count becomes bounded`. The scoped test fails in test/retry.test.mjs. H5 passes, H6 commits E. The exception lands and is named in the spec's `## Rework record` `Changes:`. Then P, T, R. | `merge: eeeeeee, 1 file(s) resolved, scoped tests red in test/retry.test.mjs: node --test test/retry.test.mjs` | | failure | H1–H4 run; the helper returns `done`. H5 fails: the status delta includes README.md, outside the list. Run HX: abort succeeds and HEAD = A. Task 1 is deferred to the spec. The worktree's weakened AGENTS.md is ignored. `git -C ROOT show B:AGENTS.md` is the authoritative read, so "no unbounded retries" binds the spec. Then P, T, R. | `merge: unresolved - src/retry.ts` | | credentials | H1 finds the runner has requires credentials: true, so SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS = none and the tuple's command is replaced. The helper runs nothing. H5 passes, H6 commits E. Then P, T, R. | `merge: eeeeeee, 1 file(s) resolved, scoped tests none run (requires credentials: true)` | | missing-runner | H1 finds only `npm test`, a full-suite script. File scope is never inferred, so SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS = none. The helper runs nothing. H5 passes, H6 commits E. Then P, T, R. | `merge: eeeeeee, 1 file(s) resolved, scoped tests none run (no file-scoped runner; npm test is full-suite)` | ## End state Every row ends with P passing and the R report emitted. Each row then hands W to gather and spec. The base merge and its conflict helper's scoped tests are the only pre-approval writes and runs. Nothing is pushed.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved: After keeps every fact Before kept. M is still `git -C W merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main`, no-op makes no commit with the exact record, clean names eeeeeee as the first rework commit; H4 dispatches one fresh foreground implementer at cwd W with the full tuple, H5 enforces empty U / staged src/retry.ts / contained delta, H6 has the orchestrator commit --no-edit, HX aborts with git -C W, the cwd-stays-at-other point is stated up front, overrides and AGENTS.md are read from B via ROOT, and credentials/missing-runner record specific reasons without inferring scope from npm test. Two things are weaker than Before and worth tightening so they don't slip in a later rewrite: the exception-red row says the exception is 'named in Changes' but no longer quotes the name there (Before wrote 'as "retry count becomes bounded"'), and H4 says the helper runs 'exactly those commands' while credentials/missing-runner later replace them with none — say 'runs only the dispatched SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS, which may be none'. The added T (threads query) is outside this case's scope (threads are partitioned into pr-head-threads) and is the kind of extra step that could later read as a tracker call; if the routing change requires mentioning it, keep it as a single legend line as you did rather than per-row actions. Otherwise the pr-head routing sentence at the top delivers the Change without disturbing the base-merge facts.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept: the merge command, no-op/clean records, fresh foreground implementer with the exact tuple, staging/empty-U/containment checks, orchestrator-only commit --no-edit, git -C W for discovery/status/staging/completion/commit/abort with session cwd unchanged in done-green, ROOT-targeted repository reads, accurate green/red/none records with specific reasons, abort → unresolved src/retry.ts → Task 1, BASE_SHA AGENTS.md read after every outcome, and the preapproval boundary. The one soft spot is the 'authority' fact: Before said the runner is read from the 'first-found fetched-base runner contract, not conflicted-tree instructions'; After's 'Where a BASE_SHA overrides file is specified, run git -C ROOT show B:.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md' drops both 'first-found' and the explicit contrast with the conflicted tree, and it adds an inferred failure-row runner outcome (none) that the input does not describe. To stay safe while keeping the compact-legend change, restore the phrase 'read the first-found overrides at BASE_SHA, never the conflicted tree's copy' in the Runner discovery cell and leave the failure row's runner unspecified rather than resolving it to none.
